key_insight: An NLP pipeline that reads radiology reports can identify brain metastases more completely than cancer registries, including many asynchronous cases that are usually missed.
clinical_relevance: This could support population-level surveillance and faster registry capture of brain metastases across large health systems.
method: Trained two Bio_ClinicalBERT models separately on the Findings and Impressions sections of brain/head radiology reports.
Combined section-level outputs by taking the highest predicted probability as the report-level prediction.
Validated the model internally and externally using reports from Alberta, Ontario, and British Columbia.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 1,879 samples and internally tested on 1,833 reports from 357 patients, reaching 0.888 sensitivity at a 0.4 threshold; external sensitivity was 0.918 in Ontario and 0.726 in British Columbia.
watch_item: Precision was modest and performance varied by province, so local calibration and workflow integration will be important before deployment.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
